articleTitle: Comparation of Different Rotor Sleeves of Highspeed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on Multi-physics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: For high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), since the permanent magnets (PM) cannot withstand the huge centrifugal force during high-speed rotation, alloy or carbon fiber (CF) sleeve is usually used to protect the PM. However, due to the different physical properties of CF and alloy, the sleeve will greatly affect the multi-physics performance of high-speed motors. Therefore, in order to obtain more reasonable sleeve parameters, this paper focuses on the comparative of different sleeve schemes based on multi-physics, including rotor eddy current loss, rotor stress, temperature.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Stator Water-cooling System for Yokeless and Segmented Armature Axial Flux Machine
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper deals with the stator cooling structure of yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) axial flux machine. An innovative direct water-cooling system is presented to enhance the heat transfer performance of the YASA stator. Three types of water channel structures are compared to verify their thermal performance by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation. The results show that the proposed stator cooling system can improve the temperature of the stator significantly, and the water channel Structure C of three structures can achieve the best cooling performance.

articleTitle: Thermal Design and Simulation of winding cooling for permanent magnet synchronous motor of electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the new energy vehicle “battery, motor, electronic control” three horizontal technology development layout system, motor as the core component of electric energy and mechanical energy conversion, its performance is directly related to the vehicle performance. It is one of the ways to solve the problem of high power density of electric vehicle motor that the heat of end winding is rapidly derived by heat pipe heat transfer technology to reduce the temperature rise of motor. The assembly process of heat pipe was designed. The finite element model and temperature field simulation of the two motors were established by ANSYS fluent, and the prototype was made for further test. The test results show that: the simulation results are close to the test results of the prototype, the high temperature region is located at the end of the winding, and the motor design of the cooling system with heat pipe can effectively reduce the temperature rise of the motor, which puts forward a new idea for the heat dissipation design of PMSM for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Variable Parameter PI Control based on Fuzzy Logic Strategy for Dual-Winding PMSM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper investigates a dual-winding PMSM system based on a winding reconfiguration topology. At low speed region, the motor works in winding series mode, and at high speed region, it works in winding parallel mode. However, the speed and torque fluctuation caused by dual-winding reconfiguration of the PMSM leads to decline of control system stability. This paper presents a fuzzy-logic control (FLC) for the dual-winding PMSM. This strategy can adjust the PI parameters of speed loop adaptively according to the winding state and speed error. Compared with the fixed gain PI controller. FLC reduces the speed fluctuation during winding reconfiguration process. The experimental results show the validity of the FLC.

articleTitle: Investigation of Variable Flux Memory Machines with Hybrid Connected Delta-Type Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A delta-type permanent magnet (PM) variable flux memory (VFM) machine operated with a simple hybrid-connected magnetic circuit (HMC) is investigated. The presented HMC VFM machine integrates the merit of stable PM working point in series-connected VFM machines and the easy magnetization state regulation in parallel-connected VFM machines. Moreover, it is found that the iron bridge between the two kinds of the PMs plays an essential role on magnetic hybridization ratio and thus the electromagnetic performance. The effects of the iron bridge are investigated in detail based on the theoretical analysis and finite element (FE) simulation. The results indicate that the hybridization ratio is a key consideration in the design of HMC VFM machines.

articleTitle: Thermal and Stress Analysis for a High-speed Permanent Magnet Motor with Solid Rotor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper provides the thermal and rotor strength analyses of a high-speed permanent magnet motor (HSPMM) with solid type permanent magnet rotor. The computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is used to estimate the HSPMM's thermal performances. Several water cooling methods are compared to find the more effective cooling method for the motor. Both analytical and FEM methods are employed to investigate the rotor strength performances for the HSPMM. Moreover, several factors influencing the rotor strength performances are also further studied and researched.

articleTitle: Multi-mode Drive Control System of Switched Reluctance Motor Based on a Novel $\mathrm{N}+2$ Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-mode drive control system for 12/10-pole switched reluctance motor. The drive control system can operate in the six-phase mode, three-phase serial, and parallel operation mode by altering the control signals based on a novel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}+2$</tex> power converter and it can decrease torque ripple and copper consumption by switching to the three-phase serial mode and expand the speed range by switching to the three-phase parallel mode. The mode-switching control scheme and simulation are performed to validate the proposed multi-mode drive scheme.

articleTitle: Design of Synchronous Reluctance Motors with Asymmetrical Flux Barriers for Torque Ripple Reduction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Synchronous reluctance (REL) motors have attracted increasing attention for high performance applications. However, REL motors can be vulnerable to high toque ripple if they are not properly designed. In this paper, a solution for reducing torque ripple of REL motors is presented. The rotors with one flux-barrier per pole is taken into consideration and the flux-barrier end angles are carefully selected. Formulas of the torque are derived and the optimal flux-barrier angle set for minimizing the torque ripple is obtained using the proposed analytical model. In addition, the slot effects are considered in the analytical model. Finally, the influence of the flux-barriers end angles on torque ripple is examined by using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) which aims to verify the analytical results.

articleTitle: Comparison of Rotor Strength of Various Rotor Structures for Ultra-high-speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The mechanical reliability of the rotor is the premise of the stable operation of high-speed motors, and for ultra-high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), sterner requirements are placed on the mechanical reliability of the rotor. In this paper, the rotor strength of four rotor structures of ultra-high-speed PMSMs are compared. Combining the rotor sleeve materials and the PM mechanical structures, the rotor stresses of the four rotor structures under different influencing factors are compared by 3D finite element method, and the influence of temperature, interference fit and sleeve thickness on the stresses of different rotor structures are summarized. Then, the stresses of the four rotor structures are analyzed under different operating states. Finally, based on the above analysis, some important conclusions are obtained.

articleTitle: Detection of Ending Winding Wear Regulation Acting by Electromagnetic Force in Synchronous Generators under both SISC and SAGE Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a completed investigation on the electromagnetic force characteristics of the stator end windings under stator inter-turn short circuit (SISC) conditions. Not only the single SISC or static air-gap eccentricity (SAGE) case are considered, but also takes the combined impact of SISC and SAGE condition into account at the same time. The entire work depends on the theoretical analysis and finite element method (FEM) verification. It is found that the electromagnetic force will be increased tremendously when SISC happens, particularly at 2nd, 4th and 6th harmonics. The nose and the joint between the line part and the end part on the short circuit windings are the most dangerous positions to suffer the insulation wearing.

articleTitle: The Structure of Symmetrical Stator Core Offset to Reduce Cogging Torque
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor, the interaction of the permanent magnet magnetic field and the stator slot cause cogging torque, which will affect speed ripple and operation noise. To effectively reduce the cogging torque, this paper proposes a new structure of stator, adding specific rotation angle of the symmetric stator core, namely the symmetrical stator core offset. The rationality of the structure is verified by mathematical derivation and finite element simulation with the dual-rotor and dual-stator axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor.

Author Keywords: axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Calculation of the Core Loss of High-Frequency High-Voltage Transformer Considering the Influence of Temperature
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, a finite element analysis (FEA) method based on complex permeability is proposed to analyze the eddy current loss and hysteresis loss of the ultra-thin strip wound magnetic core, which is used in high-frequency highvoltage (HFHV) transformers. The coefficients of the complex permeability are expressed as temperature equations to simulate the influence of temperature on the core loss. By layering the iron core, the problem of uneven magnetic flux distribution in the strip-wound core is solved. The experimental results are in good agreement with the simulation, and the errors between them are less than 5.1%.

articleTitle: An Enhanced SVPWM Method of Suppressing Common-Mode Voltage in Dual Three-Phase Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The common-mode voltage (CMV) in voltage-source PWM inverters is harmful to motor drive systems. An enhanced space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) method based on the careful selection of intermediate vectors is proposed in this paper, aiming at the modulation range improvement whilst the CMV suppression in dual three-phase drive systems. The intermediate vectors are synthesized by large/small voltage vectors and a higher linear modulation range can be obtained compared with the existing method. The theoretical analysis and simulation results are presented to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study on Control Strategy for PMSM Fed by Differential Boost Inverter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A three phase differential boost inverter is used in this paper to drive a permanent magnet synchronous motor. Each phase voltage of this kind of inverter can be divided into AC component plus DC bias, making the output line voltage a three-phase symmetrical sinusoidal voltage, so as to achieve permanent magnet motor drive. Compared with conventional cascaded topology composed of a DC-DC boost circuit and a voltage source inverter, the inverter only needs one-level topology to achieve boost inverter, thus has higher efficiency and lower cost. The output voltage of the inverter is sine wave instead of PWM wave, which makes it possible to drive a motor connected with a long cable. In this paper, the main circuit parameters of the three-phase differential boost inverter are designed, sliding mode control and MTPA method are used to drive a permanent magnet machine. The feasibility of this scheme is verified by Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Current-Loop Bandwidth Extension for PMSM Servo System Based on SiC Inverter and FPGA
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The current-loop bandwidth should be extended to improve the dynamic performance of the servo system. Based on the mathematical model, it is proved that the digital system delay is the main limitation factor for the current-loop bandwidth. Using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> power device, a platform of PMSM servo system is established to improve switching frequency. This paper proposes a piecewise and instant PWM update method based on FPGA, which effectively reduces digital delay. Experiments on different conditions are performed, to verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Coupled Thermo-Mechanical Stress Analysis of Insulation in Deep-Sea Oil-Filled Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Compared with normal electrical machines, deep-sea oil-filled (DSOF) motors operate in high pressure environment, which will lead to a great change of coupled thermo-mechanical stress (TMS) distribution and further influence insulation lifetime. This paper proposes an analytical model for TMS analysis of stator insulation in DSOF motors considering the impact of high pressure in deep sea environment. The finite element analysis models for motor temperature distribution and TMS analysis were established and the accuracy of the proposed analytical model was demonstrated. And it can be concluded that comparing with the motors working in normal environment, the TMS on insulation of DSOF motors is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: A Current Harmonic Suppression Method of PMSM Based on Resonant Controller and Asymmetric-SVPWM Strategy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Resonant controllers can be utilized in the variable frequency control system of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) to suppress the current harmonics for its capacity on extracting signals of specific frequency. However, the performance of resonant controllers on high-order harmonics suppression can be weakened by the limited bandwidth of the control system. This paper improves the space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) algorithm to the asymmetric-SVPWM (ASVPWM) algorithm and combine it with resonant controllers to expand the system bandwidth and promote the performance of resonant controllers on suppressing high-order harmonics.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of Single Phase Induction Motor with Copper Rotor Based on Improved Polyhedron Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Single-phase asynchronous motor needs only a single-phase power supply in operation, which has the advantages of convenient operation, simple structure, and low cost. Widely used in household small power electrical appliances. However, the efficiency of single-phase asynchronous motors is generally low. The single-phase induction motor rotor adopts a copper strip-rotor, which can not only improve the efficiency of the motor but also avoid the problem of copper casting. However, it will make the starting torque of the motor smaller and the starting current larger. To solve this problem, and improved polyhedron algorithm is proposed to optimize the motor. Firstly, the Taguchi algorithm is used to reduce the dimension of the motor. Then, taking the starting torque multiple and the starting current multiple as targets, the objective function is determined by the response surface method. Finally, the regular polyhedron algorithm with weight coefficient is used to optimize the motor and the final optimization parameters of the motor are obtained. The results show that the algorithm can improve the optimization accuracy and the motor performance is more ideal. Finally, through the prototype production, the optimization effect is verified, which has a certain engineering significance.

articleTitle: Synchronous Optimal Torque PWM with Low Torque Ripple under Low Carrier Ratio
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: High speed permanent magnet synchronous motors (HSPMSMs) are gaining more attention due to their appearing features such as high power density, high efficiency and wide speed range. However, the carrier ratio of switching frequency over HSPMSM operating frequency is relatively low and even less than 10. It causes large torque ripple, which reduces the performance and even lifetime of HSPMSM. Since the synchronous modulation strategy is preferred to reduce harmonics under low carrier ratio, the intrinsic effect of synchronous modulation on torque is revealed by deriving torque equation and a synchronous optimal torque PWM (SOTP) with low torque ripple is proposed, which is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Effect of Rotor Interturn Short circuit degree and position on Stator Circulating Current inside Parallel Branches in Generators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis on the stator circulating current inside parallel branches (CCPB) under different rotor interturn short circuit (RISC) degree and positions. Firstly, based on the characteristics of the air gap magnetic field variation before and after RISC, the specific analytical expressions of the magnetic flux density (MFD), and the CCPB of the stator are derived. Then, taking the SDF-9 generator as the research object, the finite element analysis (FEA) is used to verify the circulation characteristics of the stator CCPB under different RISC degree and positions. Finally, the results are compared with the theoretical analysis, and the two changing trends are basically consistent. It is shown that the occurrence of RISC will cause even harmonic circulation components and the 2nd harmonic is the main component. As the degree of short circuit increases, the amplitudes of even harmonic circulation components of CCPB will show an increasing trend. In addition, the amplitude of the even harmonic circulation of the stator CCPB changes with position at the same short circuit degree.

articleTitle: Analysis of Flux Leakage in Slot and Circulating Current Loss of PMSM with Concentrated Winding
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, the distribution of flux leakage in the slot of concentrated winding permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) under different conditions is analyze. And the circulating current loss of PMSM is investigated, whose armature windings consist of parallel wires. First, for a 12-slot 10-pole motor with concentrated winding, the distribution of flux leakage in the slot is studied. Then, the impact of the loss caused by the circulating currents in the parallel armature wires is estimated by finite element analysis (FEA). Additionally, the circulating current loss is reduced by transposing and reducing the number of parallel conductors. Finally, the temperature rise experiment of a 12-slot/ 10-pole motor proves the effectiveness of the FEA.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of a Hybride Excitation Flux-Switching Motor with Water-Cooling System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, to verify the heat dissipation reliability of a new hybrid excitation flux-switching (HEFS) motor, finite element is used to develop a thermal simulation method of electromagnetic-fluid-thermal coupling. First, general methods of motor temperature analysis and topology of new HEFS motor are introduced. Then, based on motor efficiency map, the maximum loss working status of HEFS motor is analysed to calculate the motor loss, which mainly includes copper loss, iron loss and eddy current loss of permanent magnet. Meanwhile, airflow field and water flow field are analysed respectively to calculate the convective heat transfer coefficient of water-cooling motor. With motor loss and convective heat transfer coefficient, the temperature of motor components at rated condition, maximum loss and maximum effciency are checked to ensure the safety of motor operation, which is also significant to further improve motor performance.

articleTitle: Mechanical properties of transformer insulations under DC bias condition
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In a traditional vibration model of transformer windings, the insulations are regarded as a linear spring. However, the windings are subjected to dynamic electromagnetic forces during operations. The electromagnetic force has a low frequency component of 50 Hz under the condition of DC bias. In this study, the dynamic mechanical properties of the insulations are extracted from the collected stress and strain data, and a Bouc-wen model is selected to fit the sequential data. In the experiment, a new platform was designed to acquire the stress and strain of the insulations under sinusoidal forces at different frequencies. It is proved that the stiffness and damping are the function of the clamping force. The mechanical parameters of the insulations under normal conditions are different from those under DC bias.

articleTitle: A Capacitance Matrix Expansion Method for Parasitic Capacitance Extraction of Excitation Winding
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The excitation voltage regulator is connected to the excitation winding of the generator to regulate the output power of the generator. The excitation winding is multicircuit winding with multi layers and multi turns. The parasitic capacitance is significant, and it leads to some problems, such as current overshooting and switching losses of the excitation voltage regulator. Therefore, the extraction of the parasitic capacitance of the excitation winding is necessary. A capacitance matrix expansion method is proposed in this paper. The matrix of the parasitic capacitance of the excitation winding is obtained. Due to the symmetric arrangement of the excitation winding, the capacitance matrix can be divided into many parts. The capacitance values of each part approach to a constant which is called the typical capacitance value. The full capacitance matrix is deduced according to the typical capacitance values. After the full capacitance matrix being transformed and simplified, the lumped parasitic capacitance of the excitation winding can be extracted. This method can both take the most advantage of the flexibility of FEA and avoid the unaffordable hardware requirement when extracting the parasitic capacitance of the multicircuit windings. The simulations and experiments are performed for the validation of this method.

articleTitle: A Modified Method for Initial Rotor Position Detection of Brushless DC Motor Based on Voltage Vector Injection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to realize the rapid detection of initial rotor position of permanent magnet brushless DC motor (BLDCM) and reduce the application cost, an improved method of initial position of the motor rotor detection is proposed by combining the salient polarity and magnetic saturation of the motor itself. By successively injecting three voltage vectors into the motor winding and collecting the DC side current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i_{\text{dc}}$</tex> at the specified time, the terminal voltage comparison circuit is also designed to compare the magnitude relationship between the inactive phase terminal voltage of c or b and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{\text{dc}}/2$</tex> under the action of effective vector, which can quickly and accurately judge that the motor rotor position is actually in a 30 degree sector. The feasibility and correctness of the proposed method are verified by the experiments.

articleTitle: A Position Control Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Controller Considering Parameter Variations of Harmonic Drive Gear Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The accuracy of position control is of great importance in industrial robot application. However, the control performance of traditional model-based methods is limited by the parameter variations and uncertainties. Therefore, when the harmonic drive gear undergoes load torque disturbances, the underdamped vibration will be generated in the link and a steady-state error will be existed in the system. In this case, a backstepping control structure based on active disturbance rejection controller is proposed. According to the method, additional feedback of link variables is introduced by the backstepping control to improve the system damping. In the meantime, torque disturbances, parameter variations and unmodeled dynamics are integrated and observed by the extended state observers. The observation errors can be sharply decayed and converged to zero with proper poles assigned. Combined with the feedforward compensation, the steady-state error is significantly reduced. The effectiveness of the method is validated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Novel Stator Resistance Online Identification method based on ADRC
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The strong coupling and nonlinear characteristic of PMSM make the traditional PID control cannot meet the demand of the precise control. Therefore, auto disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is proposed to deal with the nonlinearity, which is based on the PMSM mathematical model, and requires precise motor parameters. In this paper, a novel stator resistance online identification algorithm for PMSMs based on auto disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is proposed. By means of the characteristic of observing disturbance, the extended state observer (ESO) is used to identify the real-time stator resistance, in which the change of resistance can be taken as the disturbance. The simulation is accomplished based on Matlab/Simulink and the effectiveness is verified compared with other online identification methods.

articleTitle: Short-term Frequency Support Method for a Single-stage Photovoltaic Generator based on Residual Voltage Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: At present, PV generation has made encouraging developments with short-term frequency support technology suppressing the disturbance of frequency without external energy storage. However, it is urgent for PV generators to deal with the second drop in frequency when the capacitor runs out and loses support capability. This paper proposed a residual voltage control based short-term frequency support method for a single-stage PV generator. The residual voltage of the capacitor is controlled by considering the actual DC voltage to calculate the voltage reference, besides the difference between the actual frequency and its reference. Consequently, the capacitor can achieve a smooth transition of the voltage before exhausted. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated with EMTP-RV generated data, considering different frequency drop and capacitance of the PV generator. The results indicate that the proposed method can achieve a better frequency nadir without a second frequency dip.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Integrated Starter-Generator Based on Brush DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The conventional brushless integrated starter-generator used for the power supply system is driven by the power electronic converter, which would be composed of many controllable electronic switching devices in parallel when the system runs in high current conditions. As a result, it complicates the structure and control of the system, occupies the limited volume, and increases cost. Thus, a novel integrated starter-generator based on a conventional brush DC motor is proposed in this paper. It changes the concentrated stator winding of the DC motor to a distributed winding. At starting mode, the machine uses the stator winding as field winding and adopts an electric brush for commutation. At generating mode, the machine uses the rotor winding as field winding, and a slip ring is used to provide a DC excitation current. In this way, the machine can function as a DC motor and a synchronous generator. The basic structure and working principle of the machine are described in detail, and the feasibility of the scheme is verified by finite element analysis (FEA) results.

articleTitle: A Novel Complex Vector Decoupling Control Method of IPMSM with Fuzzy Strategy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper establishes a novel complex vector decoupling control (NCVDC) for MTPA of interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs). Then, combined with fuzzy strategy, a novel fuzzy complex vector decoupling control (NFCVDC) method is further proposed. Compared with the traditional complex vector decoupling control, the NCVDC model and the NFCVDC method are more flexible in the selection of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d-q$</tex> axis current regulator parameters. Considering the parameter variation under different load conditions, the fuzzy strategy is adopted to adaptively adjust decoupling terms and compensation terms to increase the robustness of the system. Simulation results confirm that the proposed NFCVDC method improves dynamic response performance of the current loop and has low dependence on motor parameters.

articleTitle: A New System for Calibrating a Pulsed Field Magnetometer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To obtain the accurate magnetic properties of the rare earth permanent magnet with high coercivity, a new system for calibrating a pulsed field magnetometer (PFM) is developed. A set of calibration methods is proposed to calibrate the field and magnetization of the PFM. The field is calibrated by using a Rogowski coil and a calibrated pick-up coil. A measurement system is designed and used to measure the magnetization. The signal of the measurement system is calibrated by using the pure nickel sample and the pure copper sample. The samples of iron, nickel, ferrite and NdFeB are measured, and the experimental results show the PFM calibrated by this system has good measurement performance.

articleTitle: Influence of Virtual Pole on Electromagnetic Characteristics and Equivalent Pole Pitch of Modular-secondary PMSLM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The unit-secondary of the modular-secondary permanent magnet synchronous linear motor (PMSLM) forms a continuous magnetic circuit with its adjacent spacing, which has the effect of virtual pole. According to the relationship between the pole pitch of virtual poles (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{v}}$</tex>) and the pole pitch of unit-secondary (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex>), the two kinds of combinations of modular-secondary PMLSM can be defined. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{v}}$</tex> affects the electromagnetic characteristics, which is an important parameter to be resolved and optimized. The difference between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{v}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex> leads to an equivalent pole pitch (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{e}}$</tex>) for the whole motor. The solution method of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{\mathrm{e}}$</tex> has influence on the average value and ripple of thrust and normal force. Finally, a modular-secondary PMLSM prototype conforming to the first kind of combination is developed and verified by experiments.

articleTitle: General Analysis of Combinations of High Frequency Injected Auxiliary Coils in Displacement Sensorless Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: For the traditional high frequency (HF) injection methods of bearingless motors, the HF signal is always injected into the armature winding, resulting in large suspension and torque ripples. In order to solve this problem, a general theory of combinations of HF injected auxiliary coils is presented in this paper. This theory aims to eliminate certain harmonics based on the vector superposition theory of the basic excitation vector, and can be employed for bearingless motors of all pole pairs combinations with concentrated windings. It has advantage of less influence on the suspension and torque control. This theory is implemented on a 12-tooth motor, and the correctness is verified by the simulation results using Ansoft.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Rectifier for Bidirectional Electric Vehicle Chargers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the automobile industry has continued its focus towards developing all electric vehicles (EV). This has caused new EV charger technology to emerge, such as bidirectional chargers with vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-home capabilities. This paper presents a 20 kW grid connected three-phase active front end (AFE) rectifier for bidirectional EV application. The control strategy is based on voltage oriented control (VOC), which is used to supply the EV with a constant DC voltage. Calculations in the control circuit are done in the synchronous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${dq}$</tex>-reference frame, and a phase locked loop (PEL) is used to extract the phase angle from the grid. Space vector modulation (SVM) with symmetrical zero states is used for pulse width modulation of the gating pulses. A LCL filter is selected for attenuating switching harmonics. The complete topology is simulated in Simulink and is tested with an increasing load during rectification, inversion and bidirectional operation.

articleTitle: Research on Predictive Current Suspension Control of Permanent Magnet Bearingless Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper develops a suspension predictive control method for bearingless motor. Predictive control is used to replace traditional PI control for bearingless motor suspension. This paper first deduces the mathematical model of the predictive current suspension controller, and then the system simulation is carried out. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can make the rotor levitation more quickly and stably, and has better dynamic index, and realizes the decoupling of motor suspension control and torque control.

articleTitle: Modular Converter-Based Predictive Current Control of SRM for Torque Ripple Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a deadbeat predictive current control to minimize the torque ripple for switched reluctance motor (SRM) drives based on the standard switching modules. The voltage duty ratio required to reach the reference current is accurately predicted by the developed predictive control, which can effectively suppress the torque ripple issue caused by the conventional two-phase series excitation scheme. Based on the current distribution characteristics of torque sharing function (TSF), the novel excitation, freewheeling and demagnetization modes are flexibly configured to make full use of the torque capability of each phase. The actual current can track the reference more accurately and the torque ripple is effectively minimized. Meanwhile, the adopted fixed switching frequency can help to achieve the uniform distribution of power loss for heat balance design and the minimized audible noise. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, the simulation is carried out on a 150W, three-phase 12/8 SRM.

articleTitle: Research on Minimum Switching Loss SVPWM Control of Dual Three-Phase PMSM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Switching loss is an important factor in the dual three-phase PMSM drive system. In this paper, a method of minimum switching loss SVPWM (MSL-SVPWM) is proposed. The switching loss equation is presented, and a switching loss calculation model is used to calculate IGBT switching loss. To reduce the switching loss of the inverter, the minimum switching loss SVPWM can distribute the zero vector and active vector reasonably, and make the inverter has three-phase bridge arm or four-phase bridge arm clamping in each switching period. To show the performance of the proposed method, the simulation and experiments are conducted and results are presented.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Current Control for Synchronous Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Synchronous-frame proportional-integral (PI) current control is the most popular solution in industrial synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) drive systems. However due to the magnetic saturation and winding temperature rise, the motor parameters(L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf> and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) vary widely, leading to deterioration of the current controller. To this end, this paper presents an active disturbance rejection current control (ADRCC) scheme for SynRM drives, which has a simple formation and is robust to machine parameter perturbations. An extended state observer (ESO) is designed to estimate the lumped disturbance in real-time. Then, the estimated lumped disturbance compensates the current loop to a first-order integral element. Meantime, the ADRCC parameters (w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> and w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) are just expressed in the desired current loop bandwidth and lumped disturbance bandwidth. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate when the parameters are mismatched, ADRCC performs better transient and steady current tracking performance compared to the PI current controller.

articleTitle: Research on the Effect of Winding Connection Modes on Radial Force and Vibration of Two-Phase SRM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Switched reluctance motor (SRM) has the advantages of stable structure, flexible and simple control. Compared with the most used three-phase switched reluctance motor in the market, two-phase switched reluctance motor has fewer switching devices, lower cost, and is more suitable to be used as a high-speed motor. The larger vibration and noise restrict its application in the field of small household appliances. The radial force is the main cause of the vibration and noise of the SRM. In this paper, the flux linkage and radial forces of different winding connection modes are compared and analyzed based on the magnetic circuit of two-phase 8/4 SRM with unequal tooth width. The radial force and vibration acceleration of NNNNSSSS and NNSSNNSS windings are simulated and tested in low-speed CCC mode and high-speed angle adjustment mode.

articleTitle: Improved PI Regulator with Integral Separation for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, an improved PI regulator is proposed for the control of permanent magnet synchronous motors. Integral separation is used to improve the dynamic performance. Moreover, to realize integral self-regulation after torque change, a load observer is introduced. When a large load variation is observed, the load torque integral changes accordingly to suppress the speed fluctuation. So the controller is more reliable. The simulation results show that the PMSM control system has stronger anti-interference ability with the proposed PI regulator.

articleTitle: Effect of Slot Number on Performances of a Single-Side Axial-Flux Permanent Magnet Generator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The use of permanent magnet generators (PMGs) for the application in the wind power generation is increasingly being used. Commonly NdFeB permanent magnets are applied in order to get the higher flux density in the airgap because of high coercivity and remanence. Good and bad performances of the PMGs are affected not only by the permanent magnets but also by the number of slots in the stator core and the permanent magnet configuration on the rotor. Four different slot numbers of 6 slots, 9 slots, 12 slots and 15 slots combined with three different configurations of 8 permanent magnet poles in each configuration are modeled and analyzed by the assist of the Ansys Maxwell software to know their effect on the performances of a single-side axial flux permanent magnet generator. The results show that the surface permanent magnet configuration provides the highest internal generated voltage, output power and efficiency followed by inset rotor with surface permanent magnet configuration and embedded tangential permanent magnet configuration. The results also show that the generator with 12 slots combined with the 8 poles surface permanent magnet configuration gives the highest efficiency of 93.479% compared to 6 slots, 9 slots and 15 slots.

articleTitle: High quality Open-circuit Fault Tolerant Control of a Bi-harmonic Seven-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: in this paper, an optimal open-circuit fault-tolerant control (FTC) strategy in stator nature reference is proposed for a bi-harmonic seven-phase permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM). For single phase open-circuited fault, the reference currents in stator natural coordinate system can be generated by using the principle of mirror symmetry. Not only the high quality of torque with low torque ripple is achieved, but also the stator copper consumption is minimized. This paper will give the detail derivation of the reference currents and verification of the results by simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Self-excitation Overvoltage of Offshore Interconnected Power System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The self-excitation overvoltage is prone to occur when an offshore interconnected power system implements the black start. This paper gives a mechanism explanation for the self-excitation overvoltage in an offshore power system. The stability analysis of the self-excitation overvoltage for single generator system model is presented with Routh criterion. Besides, a self-excitation overvoltage suppression method is proposed. In order to elaborate the phenomenon of self-excitation overvoltage and validate the performance of the proposed method, an offshore power system model is built using EMTP-RV simulator, which based on the actual data in Jinzhou offshore power system. The simulation results verify that the self-excitation overvoltage is caused by the current positive feedback between the generator reactance and cable capacitor, and the proposed methods can prevent the self-excitation overvoltage effectively.

articleTitle: Modified Fault Diagnosis Method of Power Converter in SRM Based on Bridge Current Reconstruction Scheme
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) has a bright future for its outstanding robustness and fault tolerance capability. The reliability of power converter plays a vital role in the reliability of the drive system. This paper investigated a precise fault detection method based on bridge current reconstruction. The proposed fault diagnosis method is easy to implement online, Short Circuit (SC) and Open Circuit (OC) of power transistors and their location are detected accurately and digital value makes fault feature pretty clear. There is no requirement for the number of phases and speed of SRM as well as experimental threshold. Besides, the method can take universality and dependability into account. Finally, the proposed scheme is validated by simulations.

articleTitle: An Improved Type-2 Phase-Locked Loop-Based Sliding Mode Observer for Sensorless Control of SPMSM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents an improved type-2 phase-locked loop-based sliding mode observer for sensorless control of surface-mounted permanent-magnet synchronous machines (SPMSM) to achieve accurate speed and position estimation. A phase-locked loop (PLL) scheme is widely employed in sensorless control methods due to its simple design. However, the traditional PLL has a large position error under speed dynamic operations. In order to eliminate such drawback, a type-2 PLL with revised structured is proposed to obtain the information of rotor position and speed accurately under dynamic process. In addition, the parameter tuning guidelines of the proposed type-2 PLL is provided in detail. Finally, the proposed method has been implemented by experiment on a Higale platform with a 0.2-kW SPMSM to verify the effective performance.

articleTitle: Study on Characteristics of Silicon Steel Sheet and Core of PMSM Used in Deep Sea
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The magnetization curve and magnetostriction curve are important curves reflecting the magnetic properties of the silicon steel sheet. In the deep-sea environment, the stator core will bear huge compressive stress, and the magnetic characteristics of silicon steel sheet and the iron loss of motor will change. This paper investigates the impact of the pressure on the magnetic properties of silicon steel sheets. The B-H curve of the silicon steel sheet is measured under different pressure levels. Based on the measurement results of the B-H curve, considering the coupling effect between the magnetic field and stress field, the stator core loss under different pressure is calculated.

articleTitle: Design of Consequent Pole Permanent Magnet Vernier Motor for Downhole Electric Drilling System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The downhole electric drilling tool can realize the high-efficiency and low-cost development of oil and gas resources in deep wells. As its core component, the downhole motor needs to have high torque density and high reliability. Permanent magnet vernier motor (PMVM) has simple structure and high torque density, but the traditional surface mounted permanent magnet vernier motor (SPMVM) has low power factor and poor reliability of structure. This paper proposes a consequent pole permanent magnet vernier motor (CPMVM) as the motor of downhole electric drilling system. The results show that the proposed CPMVM can improve the power factor and structural reliability.

articleTitle: Inrush Suppression Method of Transformer in an Offshore Power System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Offshore platform power system is crucial to the development and utilization of marine resources. The inrush current of transformer is not conducive to the safe and stable operation of offshore platform. In this paper, three inrush current suppression methods, including controlling closing angle, phase splitting closing and using closing resistor, are introduced and comparatively analyzed. Base on the data of a real offshore multi-platform interconnected power system, a model system is built to validate the introduced methods. The simulation is carried out using EMTP-RV generated data, considering the influence of remnant flux and connection mode of transformers. Finally, the most suitable inrush suppression method for an offshore power system is suggested.

articleTitle: Research on the Observation of the Rotor Flux Linkage Considering the Distribution of Rotor Current for Vector Control of Solid Rotor Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The vector control technology is rarely applied to solid-rotor induction motors (SRIMs) because of the parameter variations caused by the distribution of rotor current, which prevent the accurate observation of the rotor flux linkage. In this paper, the dynamic model of the SRIM considering the distribution of rotor current is established and transformed into a form which can be seen as a combination of a normal squirrel-cage induction motor model and a disturbance. Based on the transformed model, a model reference adaptive system (MRAS) based approach to observe the equivalent rotor flux linkage precisely is proposed. Simulation results are provided to show the proposed approach works on the SRIM with better accuracy than the traditional flux linkage observer.

articleTitle: On-line Suppression of Harmonic Currents Caused by Inverter Non-linearity for Sensorless Control of PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Inverter non-linearity could lead to voltage distortion, which will result in harmonics in the phase currents. This article proposes an algorithm suppressing the harmonic currents by using the gradient descent method. First, the effects of the inverter non-linearity are investigated. The analytical expressions of distorted voltages and harmonic currents are deduced. These harmonics will lead to position error and speed ripples in sensorless control system of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs). Then, the cross-product of fundamental and harmonic current vectors is calculated. The result is selected as the objective function. The fundamental current vector is constructed by phase-locked loop (PLL) and sin-wave generator. Furthermore, the harmonic currents are suppressed by minimizing the objective function. The process is realized by the gradient descent method. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Thermal Management of Open Air-cooled Induction Motor for Drilling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper deals with the thermal management of an open air-cooled induction motor for drilling. Firstly, the electromagnetic parameters and cooling structure of the motor are introduced. And a cooling improvement structure is proposed and described in detail. Secondly, the three-dimensional geometric model of the entire motor is established according to the basic geometric parameters and cooling arrangement. Then, the multi-physics field bidirectional coupling analysis is used to determine the distribution of fluid and temperature in the motor. The simulation results are discussed and analyzed in depth, and the effectiveness of the proposed structure is verified through simulation. Finally, an experiment is conducted to verify the accuracy of the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy plus Integral Composite Control Strategy of Switched Reluctance Motor for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Switched reluctance motor (SRM) has been widely developed in the field of new energy vehicles and home electrical appliances due to its advantages of simple structure, high fault tolerance, high reliability, good suitableness for harsh working conditions, and flexible control. This paper takes the switched reluctance motor used in electric vehicles as the research object. The simulation model of the system is established combined with the characteristics of the switched reluctance motor and the mechanical motion equation. Aiming at the problem that fuzzy control is easy to produce steady state error, a speed regulator of switched reluctance motor is designed based on fuzzy + integral control strategy. It is verified that the system has better dynamic response and steady-state performance after using the fuzzy + integral composite control strategy. Finally, a four-phase 16/12 switched reluctance motor used for EV is tested. The results show that the combined control strategy can effectively adjust the speed and torque of the motor, which verifies that the motor system has high robustness under different working conditions.

articleTitle: An Improved Robust Deadbeat Predictive Current Control without Computational Delay
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved robust deadbeat predictive current control (DPCC) method without computational delay for surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous machine (SPMSM). With the proposed method, the computational delay is reduced greatly, and the pulse-width-modulation (PWM) command could be updated in the sample control period with the current sample to realize one-step delay deadbeat dynamic response. A proportional-integral (PI) controller is added to the DPCC method to improve the system's robustness, which can achieve zero steady-state current error, even with inaccurate motor parameters. Compared with the conventional DPCC method, this technique has the benefits of simpler realization. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been validated by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Generalized Analysis of Armature Windings MMF Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Harmonics in magnetomotive force (MMF) composed by armature windings play an important role in reflecting the performance of an AC electric machine. With the emerging of various novel configurations of multi-layer fractional-slot and polyphase windings, whilst limited by the time-consuming calculation and lack of universality in finite element analysis (FEA), an analytical method to depict the MMF harmonics which applies to all kinds of feasible windings is in need. In this paper, a generalized MMF harmonic analysis approach, which is applicable to symmetric and asymmetric, fractional-slot and integer-slot windings, accounting for odd and even space or time harmonic orders, is proposed and expressed as closed form equations.

articleTitle: Common Mode Electromagnetic Interference Source Characteristics of SiC MOSFETs in Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, common mode electromagnetic interference source characteristics of Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs in motor drives is analyzed. The source of common mode electromagnetic interference in the motor system is the high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}v/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> of the phase voltage caused by the switching of the SiC MOSFET. This paper analyze the current commutation process to learn whether the switching of SiC MOSFETs will cause high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}v/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> of the phase voltage is determined by the gate drive signal and the direction of the load current. And then the frequency of common mode electromagnetic interference generation caused by SiC MOSFETs in motor system with SPWM is 6 times of the frequency of carrier wave is learned. Finally, in order to analyze the transient of the common mode electromagnetic interference source, the influence of DC bus parasitic inductance on common mode voltage is analyzed through theoretical analysis and simulations. The results show that the DC bus parasitic inductance will exacerbate common mode electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: Research on Correlation Analysis of Power User Behavior Based on Coupled Meteorological Factors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In recent years, large-scale power outages caused by extreme weather conditions have occurred frequently at home and abroad. Hence, how to quickly and accurately use the massive data in the power grid to mine the correlation between meteorological factors and users' consumption behavior is of great significance. Especially in assisting subsequent power dispatching decisions, improving the power grid's ability to respond to extreme weather, and ensuring the reliability of power supply for important power users. In this situation, this paper combine The Random Matrix Theory and Pearson's Correlation Coefficient Theory, to further propose a new method of data mining. Firstly, calculate and select effective coupled meteorological indicators, and then calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between the indicators and the load data. On this basis, a random matrix model is constructed, and its time-series linear characteristics such as empirical spectrum distribution conform to a variety of statistical theorems. Finally, complete the spectrum analysis, and then fully quantify the degree of coupled meteorological factors on the consumption behavior of users, and realize the effective combination of visualization and quantification. This paper aims to effectively extract the correlation characteristics, and serve for subsequent load forecasting and power system planning. The 2018 and 2019 summer data of a certain regional grid in my country are selected to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Energy-Optimal Reference Trajectory with Iterative Learning-Based Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to improve the motion performance of the servo system, a dynamic trajectory optimal strategy is proposed in this paper. Firstly, an energy-optimal S-curve trajectory planning model is constructed based on the kinematic and electrical constraints to optimal the energy consumption. Secondly, an iterative learning control method is designed to modify the referenced trajectory, through which to make the actual position of the servo system to track the designed trajectory and adjust to real-time feedback. Finally, the proposed trajectory control strategy is compared with the conventional methods by simulation. Results validate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Quantification Index of Voltage Stability Based on Physical Mechanism of Reactive Power Distribution
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the scale of the power system gradually expanding, the proportion of new energy and power electronic devices connected to the grid increases continually, making the grid structure more complex. In this situation, the reactive power distribution in the grid and its influence on static stability need further research. Hence, this paper deeply discuss the physical significance of reactive power distribution and the physical mechanism of instantaneous reactive power. Firstly, the concept of power flow tracing and the theoretical method of reactive power flow tracing are elaborated. Secondly, on the basis of the traditional nodal effective energy function model, this paper takes the influence of OLTC and reactive power injection into consideration, improving the quantitative index of power system stability based on the energy function, and the stability margin index and its change trend are also analyzed under different conditions. Next, considering the degree of reactive power coupling and the regional reactive power compensation capability, a research scheme for zonal evaluation of the robustness of system reactive power support is proposed in this paper. Finally, both the power system simulation platform and the power flow visualization package are programmed and implemented. This paper provides a more satisfactory scheme for the construction of the power system stability analysis system, and the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed indexes and scheme are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Torque Analysis and Optimization of Synchronous Reluctance Motor Shielded by Magnetic Stator Can
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Shielded motors mostly use non-magnetic cans, which reduce the output torque of the motor. Based on equivalent magnetic network (EMN) and finite element analysis, the effect of magnetic stator can on the torque performance of synchronous reluctance motor is studied in this paper. Compared with unshielded motor, the average torque is increased and the torque ripple is reduced by using suitable material and thickness of stator can. The established EMN model of shielded synchronous reluctance motor can consider the influence of motor saturation, and its calculation speed far exceeds finite element analysis, while the accuracy is not much lower. Genetic algorithm combined with EMN model is used to optimize the design of the motor stator, aiming at increasing the output torque. Finally, the accuracy and effectiveness of the optimization results are verified by the finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Maximum Inductance Detection-based Fault-Tolerant Sensorless Control for SRM Drive
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper aims at developing a filtered current gradient method for sensorless switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive under voltage PWM control. By implementing the zero-crossing point estimation algorithm of phase inductance slope, the proposed scheme can effectively avoid the interference signal caused by the advanced turn-on angle and ensure that only one position index pulse, representing the aligned position, is detected in each electric cycle. Meanwhile, a position index pulse delay strategy is developed to estimate the rotor position in real time with single-phase lacking fault-tolerant capability. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by the simulation on a 150W, three-phase 12/8-pole SRM.

articleTitle: Motor bearing fault diagnosis based on multi-feature fusion and PSO-BP
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes fault a diagnosis method based on the combination of multi-feature fusion, particle swarm optimization and BP neural network(PSO-BP). In this method, the vibration signal of motor bearing is decomposed by wavelet packet, then the fuzzy entropy of each frequency band is solved, and finally the mixed feature vector is formed with the kurtosis of the original signal, which is input into PSO-BP for fault diagnosis. The simulation experiment is carried out using bearing data from CWRU, and the results prove that this method can more effectively distinguish the types of motor bearing faults.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Inertia Control Methods for a PMSG-Based Wind Turbine Generator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With a higher wind power penetration level, the power system faces more challenges in the frequency control due to the system inertia reduction. Many papers have investigated the inertia control from variable speed wind turbines generators. In this paper, a detailed comparative analysis of inertia control methods for a permanent magnet synchronous generator-based wind turbine generator is presented. Three representative inertia control methods, including constant droop control method, time-variable droop control method, and kinetic energy-based droop control method, are described in detail, and the performance of these methods are analyzed with EMTP-RV generated data. The results show that the methods with dynamic control coefficient have a great improvement on frequency response and prevent the secondary frequency dip, effectively.

articleTitle: Rotor Unbalanced Magnetic Pull Characteristics Properties in Synchronous Generators Due to Dynamic Air-gap Eccentricity Faults
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis on the rotor UMP characteristics under dynamic air-gap eccentricity fault (DAGE) in synchronous generators. Different from other studies, this paper not only pays attention to the effect of the DAGE degree, but also considers the impact of the DAGE direction, on the rotor UMP at the meantime. In the work, the rotor unbalanced magnetic pull (UMP) model employs two primary factors, i.e., the eccentric rate and the angle between the center line of the rotor and the eccentric direction, to reflect the eccentric degree and the eccentric direction, respectively. The simulation results prove the validity of the qualitatively theoretical model on a synchronous generator. The study shows that the rotor UMP increases under the DAGE conditions and the increment of the rotor UMP is closely related to the eccentric direction.

articleTitle: Study on the Pulse Transformer with energy recovery for Repetitive Pulsed High Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As the frequency of repetitive pulses is limited by the low efficiency of the energy supplement, the scheme of multimodule power supplies which can produce the multi-pulse with tens of Hz is proposed. An energy recovery circuit main composed of a pulse transformer is used to reduce the requirements of the energy supplement. The structure of the pulse transformer with the coupling coefficient 0.6 is designed, and the inductance of primary winding and secondary winding are the same. In order to obtain the structure parameters accurately, a particle swarm optimization support vector machine (PSO-SVM) is selected to provide design principles. With the participation of the transformer, the energy conversion efficiency between the two capacitors is 66.28 %, which can save 80 % replenish time of recharging.

articleTitle: An Advanced Boost Chopper Converter-Based Direct Instantaneous Torque Control for SRMs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, an advanced boost chopper converter-based direct instantaneous torque control (DITC) is proposed for switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive with double-PI control strategy. Different from the traditional DITC method based on the hysteresis loop control, the fixed switching frequency control by the proposed PWM method is implemented instead of variable switch frequency control. Moreover, with the proposed converter, the dc-link voltage prediction and commutation torque distribution control can be implemented to effectively reduce the torque ripple during the commutation period and improve the efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by the simulation on a 150W, three-phase 12/8-pole SRM.

articleTitle: A Current Harmonic Suppression Strategy for Electrolytic Capacitor-less Drive System of PMSM Based on Resonant Controller
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the electrolytic capacitor-less (ECL) motor drive system, the armature current can contain large harmonic components due to the pulsations of DC-link voltage. Conventional ripple eliminators and control strategies utilized in ECL drivers are mainly designed for correcting the gird current and power factor but pay little attention to the current harmonics and dynamic performance of the motor side. This paper analyses the characteristics of harmonics of the motor side and effectively suppresses the current harmonics with resonant controllers.

articleTitle: Power Grid Disturbance Prediction and Analysis Method Based on SIR Model
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the continuous development of the times and the continuous improvement of people's living standards, the power system is also keeping pace with the times. At the same time, the transmission of power grid disturbance is becoming more and more obvious. If we can't analyze the power grid disturbance in the process of power grid transmission, it will lead to the chain accident of power grid or large-scale power outage of power grid. This paper mainly studies the disturbance propagation characteristics of power grid, which has an important impact on the security and stability of power system. This paper cites the mature SIR model in the field of biology and combines it with the disturbance propagation of the power grid. By analyzing the model and analogy to the disturbance propagation of the power grid, this paper analyzes the impact of the disturbance propagation of the power grid on the stability of the power system, which makes it easier to further track and locate the disturbance source and give a first warning of the degree of the disturbance of the power grid, The model simulation shows that the scheme can effectively deal with the impact of disturbance propagation and make the power system operate more safely and stably.

articleTitle: Torque Calculation of PMa-SynRM Using the Magnetic Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a torque analysis method for the design of PMa-SynRM. Firstly, an analytical model of the multilayer flux barrier structure of the rotor is established based on the magnetic equivalent circuit. To improve the calculation accuracy of the model, the effects of stator slotting and rotor magnetic bridge saturation are considered. Then, the analytical expression of the air gap flux density is derived and the output torque of the motor is calculated by the Lorentz force law, and the analysis results are verified by the finite element method. Finally, the torque performance of the motor under different flux barrier structures is compared through the analysis model.

articleTitle: Integration of a Protection/Measurement Current Transformer based on Compensation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, a compensation algorithm for the integration of a protection/measurement current transformer is proposed, which can realize the accurate measurement of the grid current in both normal and fault situations. According to a real CT data and its hysteresis curve, two hyperbolic models can be established. In this way, the compensation algorithm can properly describe the exciting current by secondary current. It can improve the primary current measurement by secondary current and the calculated exciting current. The results indicate the proposed method can improve the accuracy of the CT and the measurement error meet the IEC standard, both in small load currents and large fault current scenarios. As a result, a CT not only can be used for power system protection at fault condition, but also for current measurement at normal operation situation.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Resonance Suppression Strategy in High-Speed Compressor Drive
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Two-phase current sampling has been widely employed in high-speed compressor drive for cost consideration. Meanwhile, a common-mode (CM) filter is preferred to suppress the CM <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}v/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> introduced by switching devices. However, in such a system, CM resonance is brought into the armature currents, which deteriorates the armature currents and increases the torque ripples. This paper analyses the generation process of the CM resonance and proposes both hardware and software methods to suppress it, which are verified with simulation.

articleTitle: The State Evaluation of Power Transformers Based on Grey Target Theory And Simulated Annealing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A methodology of combining the grey target theory and simulated annealing (SA) to evaluate a transformer state is proposed. In the proposed methodology, the state evaluation model is developed from the grey target theory, and the dissolved gas analysis (DGA) data are chosen as the attributes of the model. Moreover, different weights are assigned to different attributes, and the SA is used to optimize the weights. Some engineering tested results of transformers states are used to verify the accuracy of the proposed methodology. The numerical results show the superiority of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Design of Variable Speed Constant Frequency Small Hydropower System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, the variable speed constant frequency technology is applied to the hydropower system and improved. The turbine side control system takes the speed as the control object and applies the maximum efficiency tracking control strategy (MPPT) to find the maximum output power point by changing the speed to ensure the maximum power output of the turbine; Abandoning the method of obtaining motor rotor position signal by using resolver in variable speed constant frequency small hydropower system, the speed information is calculated by using the sensorless rotor position detection method based on phase-locked loop, so as to connect the current inner loop and speed outer loop of variable speed constant frequency power generation system, combined with current decoupling control and SVPWM modulation algorithm, transmit electrical energy to the DC bus with maximum efficiency.

Author Keywords: sensorless rotor position detection module based on PLL

articleTitle: Comparison and analysis of two power topologies for four-phase SRM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Power converter topology is an important part of the switched reluctance motor drive, and it occupies an important proportion in the performance and cost of the entire SRD. The asymmetric half-bridge converter topology is the most common power converter topology, with the strongest independence between phase windings, flexible chopping mode, and simple control. The 2(N+1) converter topology reduces the switching tube on its basis, which can effectively reduce the volume of the power converter. However, at the same time it also reduces the independence of each phase. Current freewheeling and difficult demagnetization may increase the difficulty of control. Through the linear model on the chain-angle, the magnetic flux width range of the 2(N+1) converter topology under current chopping control and angle control positions is derived. In this paper, the finite element simulation of the control parameters of a four-phase 8/6 SRM is carried out on the ANSYS Maxwell simulation platform. Under the same motor model, when using an asymmetric half-bridge circuit and a 2(N+ 1) converter circuit, compare the output average torque and current waveforms at different speeds. Since the current freewheeling time of the 2(N+ 1) converter circuit is longer, the system power density is reduced. At the same time, due to the limitation of the conduction width of the 2(N+1) converter circuit, the phase current is smaller than the asymmetric half-bridge circuit, and the efficiency is slightly lower. Finally, an experimental platform was built to compare the effects of the two power converters on the performance of the motor system through experiments, and the simulation analysis verified that the simulation was correct.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of a Seven-phase Non-sinusoidal Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Using High Frequency Signal Injection Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a sensorless control strategy for seven-phase non-sinusoidal permanent magnet synchronous machine (NSPMSM) with high frequency signal injection (HFSI) method in 5th harmonic subspace. Seven-phase nonsinusoidal machine benefits high torque density due to the use of third harmonic components. Firstly, two torque generation strategy in different harmonic subspaces with the minimum injected rms value and amplitude of current is deduced in this paper.
